# CLAUDE.md — Inflection Alpha Pipeline

Equity research pipeline for Indian small/micro-cap GARP transition
analysis. Operator: Keerti Kaushik. Strategy: transition alpha, 25% CAGR
target, 3-5 year holds.

## NEVER
- Never use any exit PE from outside Section 1B (v3.3 base + v3.5.1 +
  v3.6 + v3.7 + v3.8 + v3.9 + v3.10 amendment layers in frameworks/; later
  layers govern overlaps). It is the sole exit multiple authority. No
  round-number defaults, ever. There is no numeric ceiling but the sector
  cap; "never above 20x" language is void (v3.10 Amendment 26.5).
- Never anchor a base case to the audited past (v3.10 Amendment 26). Base
  revenue runs off the 26.1 basis hierarchy, with historical CAGR shown as
  the cross-check and used as the base only when no forward evidence
  exists. Base margin runs off the 26.2 destination-mix bridge; the
  trailing 3-year average is the BEAR input, except for margin-reset names,
  where the bear margin comes from the evidence bridge (operator ruling
  OR-11, approved 2026-09-28). Weights key to the trailing
  four quarters of Role 5 delivery, never whole-company history.
- Never shade an input to be safe. State the most evidenced path, name the
  two readings and the one observation that separates them, and put the
  conservatism in position size (v3.10 Amendment 26.3; v3.9 Amendment 25
  sets size as the margin of safety for fast-growth names; OR-31). This binds Role 1
  projections; it does not touch the document-reading protocols, where
  conservative interpretation of filed evidence still stands.
- Never construct a Year-N exit price on a different earnings basis than
  the entry, and never carry a within-hold option slice into the exit as
  an unresolved probability (v3.8 Amendment 18).
- Never present an entry zone without the Amendment 19 FV CAGR and
  return-source classification; an entry discount is only interpretable
  against how fast fair value itself grows.
- Never deliver a Role 2, Role 6, or FTTCP output without the
  Second-Order Section (Master v3.7 Rule F). Five linkage chains minimum,
  each with a labelled [INFERENCE]. A chain with no inference is a
  summary. Live-web links this container cannot reach are marked PENDING
  LIVE VERIFICATION and named, never fabricated.
- Never run Role 3 against a bull case that was not built to depth
  (Master v3.7 Rule H). Confirm the forward basis, the margin bridge, five
  chains, and a filled Entrepreneur Ledger first. If one is missing, STOP
  and return to Role 2. A devil's advocate against a thin bull is void.
- Never treat building as a footnote to governance (Master v3.7 Rule G).
  Role 2 Section 3G ledgers what the promoter built, raised, deployed, and
  delivered under constraint, and states its Pillar 3 line. The ledger
  never lifts a cap set by a promoter AVOID or an INTEGRITY concern; for a
  STRUCTURE concern, three of four evidenced ledger heads size as TRUSTWORTHY,
  with each concern a named tripwire (operator ruling OR-14).
- Never answer a failure-catalogue pattern-match without the nearest
  success name and the observable difference (Master v3.7 Rule I). While
  frameworks/success_catalogue.md holds fewer than four names, say
  "success catalogue pending" and continue.
- Never be a cheerleader, and never be a coroner (Master v3.7 Rule J). A
  bull claim and a bear claim carry the identical bar: tier the evidence,
  trace the chain, name the confirming observation. Depth is the default;
  if the operator has to say "go deeper", the output failed.
- Never produce a Role 1 valuation without the Section 1A Method
  Suitability Matrix and method triangulation; the Section 1B destination
  PE governs the exit multiple, it does not replace method selection.
- Never feed spot-year ROCE or rupee-denominated WC trends into Section
  1B or FTTCP for a CONVERTER-classified name (v3.7 Amendment 17).
- Never halt a run on company quality. Flags propagate; only mechanical
  failures halt. There is no STOP verdict; the verdict set is PROCEED /
  PROCEED WITH CAVEATS / PROCEED WITH FLAGS / REWORK / INSUFFICIENT
  EVIDENCE.
- Never let INDETERMINATE cash conversion silently resolve to PROCEED.
  It caps at PROCEED WITH CAVEATS with the missing evidence named.
- Never treat low institutional ownership as a risk. UA multiplier per
  Amendment 3: min(Raw x 1.25, Sector Cap), all three qualifiers evidenced.
- Never conflate the Emerging Moat scan (stage 7) with FTTCP (inside
  stage 11). Separate analyses, separate names.
- Never estimate a missing number. NOT FOUND is the only valid fill.
- Never credit one quality improvement through two mechanisms.
- Never write X posts here. Publish candidates are flagged only.
- Never let a maker verify its own work. Verifiers get fresh contexts
  and artifact paths only.
- Never emit a final synthesis or Notion payload without the
  BUSINESS UNDERSTANDING NARRATIVE (five questions, prose, before the
  verdict card). A verdict without understanding is a shallow summary;
  the operator reads the narrative first.
- Never run /fttcp or any valuation on an unsigned Mental Model
  Declaration or a Halt 1 decision other than PROCEED.

## DISPATCH (model per subagent, already set in .claude/agents frontmatter)
- claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5), effort xhigh: stage 11 valuation, stage 15
  devil's advocate, verifiers B and C, quarterly A5, and the /fttcp session
  (start that session on Opus 5.5 at xhigh; the command pins no model)
- claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5), effort high: stage 13 synthesis, stage 14
  thesis, quarterly A3-A4
- claude-sonnet-5-5 (Sonnet 5.5), effort medium: stages 1, 4, 6, 09b,
  10 assembly, verifier D, quarterly A2; effort high (set in the file):
  verifier A; effort low: quarterly A1; default (high): stages 2, 3, 5,
  7, 8, 9
- claude-haiku-5-5 (Haiku 5.5), effort medium: stage-00-intake-check
  (stage 0 document identity and file-type check; proposes, the orchestrator
  verifies); effort high: verifier-a-shadow, one Phase 1 only, findings count
  for nothing, switch .claude/shadow.yaml (operator ruling 2026-10-11). No
  extraction stage (2, 3, 5, 7), verifier of record, synthesis or valuation
  step runs on Haiku.
- No stage runs on Haiku 4.5 (operator ruling 2026-10-04: stage 10 and
  verifier A moved to Sonnet 5.5; Verifier A's independence comes from a
  fresh context and the source page, not the model family)
Do not upgrade a stage's model without editing its agent file.
The model and effort in .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter are the operator's
rulings. A session never overrides them on the belief that the file is stale.
If the file looks stale, run the stale-checkout guard instead.

## OPERATOR RULINGS (dated; Section 1B rulings live in .claude/skills/section-1b/SKILL.md)

Post-Kwick rulings, 2026-10-04 (audits/RULINGS_2026-10.md, post-Kwick section):
- OR-32: Verifier A checks 100% of verdict-card, Section 1B pillar and
  Gate 0 inputs (mandatory_checked of mandatory_total in B12a); everything
  else stays a materiality sample with coverage stated honestly.
Housekeeping rulings, 2026-10-11 (PR #212):
- Remediation cap: one remediation cycle per Phase 1, counted in
  manifest.yaml remediation_cycles; a second is refused and goes to Halt 1 as
  an open item, the verdict standing as it is (/run-pipeline step 5b).
- Verifier re-run cap: each verifier runs once per Phase 1, counted in
  manifest.yaml verifier_runs. A re-run needs an operator approval recorded
  in inputs/operator-notes.md; the Verifier A severity-addendum re-run is
  one. The verifier re-check inside the one permitted cycle is part of the
  cycle. Mechanical re-runs (missing or empty report, malformed block) do
  not count.
- Stuck rule: every agent stops after three unchanged repeats or five turns
  with nothing new learned, reports what it tried, and writes its block with
  status: blocked. A blocked block is a finished run, never re-invoked.
- Halt 1 report: file path and at most ten summary lines per deliverable,
  never the full body in chat; it ends with "Change that would make the next
  run cheaper: ___". /finalize keeps printing its finals in full.
- session-cost.md ends with fresh tokens, re-read tokens and the re-read
  multiple. Subagent prompt cache TTL is 1h (.claude/settings.json), judged
  on that multiple in the next run.

## WORDS
- "done" for a stage = full report written AND valid YAML block emitted
- "anchored" = every number followed by (source, page/note)
- "flag" = surfaced prominently in the verdict, decision stays human

## SESSION DISCIPLINE (prompt cache)
- Model and effort are fixed at session start and never changed mid-session:
  switching either busts the prompt cache and re-prefills the whole
  conversation at full price. This governs the session's own model and is
  separate from subagent DISPATCH (each stage runs its own agent at its
  frontmatter model, which is not a mid-session switch). If a different
  session model is needed, start a fresh session.
- Run commands quiet by default so their output does not flood context on
  every use: git commit -q, git status --short, git log --oneline -n N
  (never a bare git log / git diff over a large range); pip install -q;
  apt-get install -y -qq; redirect verbose PDF-extraction output. The
  collect_to_repo.py collector runs on the operator's machine, out of
  session; in-session it appears only as collect_to_repo.py --push-again.
  Exception: /step1 runs it with --dry-run on the operator's desktop.
- Trim long command output, never documents (operator ruling 2026-10-11).
  Long shell output, test output, and build and render logs are kept to the
  first part plus a short summary. Paths, numbers and error lines stay
  exact. This rule never applies to corpus documents (annual reports,
  transcripts, filings, presentations): those are always quoted verbatim
  with page anchors.
- Sparse checkout (operator ruling 2026-10-03): a pipeline session first runs
  tools/sparse_session.sh runs/<folder> [more folders]. It keeps everything
  outside runs/, runs/_template/, every run's session-cost.md and
  manifest.yaml, and the named run folders, so the tree is about 80 MB, not
  4.8 GB. Add a folder the same way when a session needs it;
  tools/sparse_session.sh --off restores the full tree. Never run git stash or
  git reset --hard over a full checkout.
- Run tools/dry_check.sh before merging any PR that touches .claude/,
  prompts/, frameworks/ or tools/ (operator ruling 2026-10-03).
- Stale-checkout guard (operator ruling 2026-10-04): /run-pipeline, /step1,
  /fttcp, /finalize and /run-quarterly start with `git fetch origin main` and
  `git diff --quiet origin/main -- .claude/ prompts/ frameworks/ CLAUDE.md LESSONS.md`.
  A non-empty diff or a failed fetch stops the command before it reads any
  framework file. The session-start hook syncs only on the web, so on a local
  checkout this guard is the only check.
- Any session that commits a framework or prompt amendment must end by
  opening a PR to main the same day. Run outputs and framework amendments
  go in SEPARATE commits so recovery stays surgical.
- Framework/prompt amendments and run outputs travel on SEPARATE branches
  and PRs; an amendment never rides a run PR.
- Any PR that changes frameworks/, .claude/skills/section-1b/ or an operator
  ruling also updates claude-web/PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md (the claude.ai
  project instructions), or says in the PR description why not.

## FERRY AND COMMIT HYGIENE (both sides; team workflow v2)
- Hash by default. Every report a command produces that involves a commit
  ends with the commit hash and `git log -1 --stat`. Claude web verifies
  against the repo; the operator never has to ask. A commit reported without
  its hash is incomplete.
- Dependency alignment. When an edit changes a status, ruling, or gate in one
  section, align every dependent section (header status, supersessions,
  blocking list, open items) in the SAME commit, and list what you aligned.
  "Keep everything not named" never produces a file that contradicts itself.
- Self-contained ferry blocks. Any text the operator carries between Claude
  Code and Claude web contains everything needed to act on it: page IDs, file
  paths, hashes, exact replacement text. A reference to "the IDs above" or "my
  earlier message" is a defect.
- Each document is paid for once. Corpus documents are read by Claude Code;
  documents uploaded to claude.ai are read there. Neither ferries a document
  to the other.
- Every run ends with session-cost.md (see run-pipeline close-out). It travels
  with run outputs, never on the framework branch.
- Deferred work is recorded. A commit message or PR description that says
  "open action", "left for later" or "recorded as" needs a matching line in
  LESSONS.md or LESSONS_ARCHIVE.md: the commit itself changes one of those
  files, or a line names the commit's 8-character hash or the PR as "#N".
  The session-start hook runs .claude/hooks/lessons-phrase-check.py over
  commits and PRs since 2026-09-15 and reports any item without a match.
  It reports; it never blocks a session.

## MEMORY
/run-pipeline, /fttcp, /finalize, and /compost sessions read the ACTIVE
LESSONS.md at start (the lean working memory, hard budget under 1,500 tokens:
named failure catalogue, recurring patterns, promoted-to-law fixes, open
actions). Lighter sessions that do not touch pipeline operations skip it. The
full dated run history lives in LESSONS_ARCHIVE.md (never deleted), read only
by /compost and by humans. Every /run-pipeline, /fttcp, and /finalize session
appends one dated entry at close to LESSONS_ARCHIVE.md, NOT to the active
file: what broke or dragged this run, one line each; write 'clean run' if
nothing. /finalize writes that entry in the fixed table of its step 8c and
adds a LESSONS.md OPEN ACTIONS line only for rows still OPEN. LESSONS.md is
orchestrator-session memory only; no stage or verifier
subagent receives it. When /compost promotes a pattern into the active
LESSONS.md, one old active lesson is reviewed for archiving so the token
budget holds; the promotion is noted under PROMOTED TO LAW.

Per-company memory lives in companies/<TICKER>.md, written or updated at
/finalize close and read as COMPANY MEMORY by /run-pipeline stage 0 and by
/fttcp. It carries the one-line thesis, Decision Status and entry zone,
operator rulings with dates, active tripwires, the optionality register
summary, and links to every run folder for the ticker. It is memory to
weigh, never anchored evidence.

Root HANDOFF.md holds framework and housekeeping state. The main session reads
it at session start; subagents do not. Update it at each milestone and before
ending a session; delete items once closed. Keep it under 1,500 words. Run
status stays in companies/<TICKER>.md and the run manifest.

## STRUCTURE
- HANDOFF.md     framework and housekeeping state (main session only)
- prompts/       stage instructions, single source of truth
- frameworks/    Master v3.7 (file Master_Project_Prompt_v3_6.md; the path
                 is stable, the version is in the banner), Section 1B layer set
                 (v3.3/v3.5.1/v3.6/v3.7/v3.8/v3.9/v3.10),
                 FTTCP v2.3, Quarterly v1.4, AR v1.3, plus
                 success_catalogue.md (Rule I; operator fills, 0 of 4
                 names, not yet enforced) (Keerti
                 maintains; stage 11 reads the section-1b skill, so an
                 amendment here reaches stage 11 only when the matching
                 .claude/skills/section-1b/references chunk is regenerated
                 in the same commit), plus
                 Downstream_Source_Discovery_Protocol_v1_0.md (source
                 registry for downstream signal candidates; Role 5.5
                 verifies against it in claude.ai)
- claude-web/PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md   repo copy of the claude.ai project
                 instructions (v4.1); the operator pastes it into the
                 project settings and keeps the two in sync
- runs/<ticker>-<date>/   one folder per run, see runs/_template
- companies/<TICKER>.md   durable per-company memory, written at /finalize,
                 read as COMPANY MEMORY by /run-pipeline stage 0 and /fttcp
- LESSONS.md     ACTIVE operational memory (lean, <1,500 tokens), read by
                 pipeline commands at start
- LESSONS_ARCHIVE.md   full dated run history (never deleted), appended at
                 close, read only by /compost and humans
- anti-ai-writing-style.md   house style for all reader facing prose
                 (synthesis narratives, recommendations, X posts); the
                 STYLE authority the orchestrator and stage 13 cite
- Narrative_Writing_Style_v1.md   STE (ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical
                 English) plus Zinsser; the operator voice authority cited
                 by OPERATOR VOICE below and by the closing narrative
                 section of every analysis
- .claude/agents/         subagent definitions with model routing
- /run-pipeline runs/<folder>   executes everything
- /run-quarterly TICKER --docs ...   quarterly review pipeline (Role 4/5):
                 five gated agents A1 extractor -> A2 enumerator -> A3
                 forensic notes -> A4 analyst -> A5 adversary; enumeration
                 before interpretation; writes runs/<ticker>-<quarter>/work/;
                 needs the two Quarterly_*_Protocol files in frameworks/

## SPEAR GATE (spear before shield; operator ruling 28-Aug-2026)
The framework grew shield-first: verify everything, then value. Inverted by
operator ruling. A SPEAR PASS runs FIRST, on live web, by Claude web, before
any pipeline machinery. Heavy pipeline runs only on a SPEAR HIT or an explicit
operator override. The spear hands the pipeline its priority verification
targets, the load-bearing facts. Claude Code does not run the four-step
spear below. Operator ruling 2026-09-05: the /step1 intake, run by Claude
Code with live web and grounded in the corpus it collects, replaces the web
spear. It writes "Spear: OVERRIDE <date> (operator standing ruling
2026-09-05: Step-1 intake replaces the web spear)", which satisfies the gate.

The four steps:
- POND. Live-web opportunity size in numbers. How large is the market the
  business fishes in.
- CATCH. A 3-year careful/fair/dream revenue and profit guess, anchored to
  observed conversion evidence, never to hope.
- PRICE. Per-share scenario values, probability weighting, and the entry price
  that clears the 25% CAGR target.
- VERDICT. HIT / WATCH / MISS against CMP.

Gate rule. /run-pipeline and /fttcp on a new name require a line in
companies/<TICKER>.md, above the Mental Model block, in one of two forms:
- Spear: HIT YYYY-MM-DD - entry <= Rs X - load-bearing facts: [2-4 items]
- Spear: OVERRIDE YYYY-MM-DD (operator)
If neither line exists, STOP. Direct the operator to run /step1, or the spear
pass with Claude web, first. The pipeline never runs a new name shield-first.

The load-bearing facts named in the Spear line are the run's FIRST
verification priority. Stage 0 carries them; every later stage checks them
before its own work.

## PIPELINE SEQUENCE (operator-gated)
/run-pipeline (evidence, stages 0-9 + verifiers + 09b dossier) -> HALT 1:
operator reads the dossier, resolves corpus gaps, signs the Mental Model in
claude.ai, decides KILL / SHALLOW / PROCEED -> claude.ai: live
verification, verticals to depth, Role 5.5 tracker writes -> /fttcp
(deliberation) -> Role 1 valuation -> /finalize. Understanding precedes
deliberation. Deliberation precedes valuation. Nothing after Halt 1 runs on
an unsigned model.

## TEAM WORKFLOW — Claude Code and Claude web
Claude Code reads the heavy corpus once (PDFs, ARs, transcripts) and holds
the repo. Its live web is limited to WebSearch and WebFetch in /step1 and
stages 8 and 9; a failed search marks the stage partial, and nothing is
filled from memory. Claude web (claude.ai) does live
verification, cross-checks, tracker and Notion writes. It must NOT re-read
corpus documents. It asks Claude Code via operator-ferried extraction
prompts (quote-then-comment, NOT DISCLOSED allowed, filename+date
verification mandatory). Filed documents beat inference. Every claim
carries its evidence tier. The pipeline produces payloads. One approved
exception (operator ruling 2026-10-03): /run-quarterly writes Notion
in-session, only after the operator approves the printed payload in that
run, and never writes Decision Status. Otherwise claude.ai
executes writes. Each document is paid for once.
The claude.ai project carries a parallel operating manual at
project-instruction level (team_workflow_project_instructions);
web-side rules bind Claude web the same way this file binds Code. The repo
keeps the current text of that manual at team_workflow_project_instructions.md
(v2, five hand-offs: standing extraction annex at Halt 1, per-entity FTTCP and
Role 1, gate pre-rulings, hash-and-ferry hygiene). The repo copy and the
claude.ai project copy are kept in sync by the operator.

## ARCHETYPE LIBRARY (mental model declarations draw from this; extend via operator ruling only)
- Build-to-spec component maker: customer capex cycle, design-win pipeline,
  content per unit, input-cost pass-through.
- Commodity converter (Section 1B v3.7 Amendment 17 binds): spread (output
  minus input price), utilisation, cycle position, cost-curve rank.
- Brand/franchise consumer: volume growth, pricing power, distribution
  reach, gross margin, advertising efficiency.
- Order-book business (EPC/defence/capital goods): order inflow,
  book-to-bill, execution pace, working capital, margin on backlog.
- Outsourcing partner (CDMO/EMS/IT services): client concentration, wallet
  share, capacity fill, contract stickiness, price per unit.
- Licence/scarcity business: licence or quota validity, renewal risk,
  regulated price, capacity cap, entry-barrier durability.
- Lender (framework variant exists): AUM growth, NIM, asset quality
  (GNPA and credit cost), RoA and RoE.
- Platform/network: active users, take rate, unit economics per
  transaction, network density, retention.

## QUALITY LADDER (mental model Part B1 names two endpoints on this; adjust via operator ruling only)
The transition thesis is a climb up this ladder. Part B1 of the Mental Model
Declaration names the tier the business LEAVES (FROM) and the tier it CLAIMS
to reach (TO), per line where lines transition differently. Rungs run low to
high. Each rung is defined by pricing power and by ROCE durability, not by
size. A business can sit between rungs; "fits no rung" is a finding, not a
gap to paper over. Per-archetype the rung labels specialise (a lender's ladder
runs on asset quality and RoA, not product spec); declare the specialised rung
where the archetype needs it. The Section 1B footprint on each rung is a
NEIGHBOURHOOD, not a computed number: Stage 11 derives the actual destination
PE from the framework; the rung only says where on the ladder that number
should land.
- R0 NON-OPERATING / ACCOUNTING-DRIVEN. Earnings not from an operating
  business (revaluations, one-offs, holding relics). No operating destination
  PE; SOTP/NAV or floor treatment. A transition FROM here must first prove an
  operating engine exists.
- R1 COMMODITY PRICE-TAKER. No pricing power; ROCE cyclical around cost of
  capital; cash volatile. ~12x neighbourhood.
- R2 COST-ADVANTAGED CONVERTER. Margin from cost position, not price; durable
  mid-teens ROCE; Amendment 17 converter multiple caps converter slices.
  ~15-17x neighbourhood.
- R3 VALUE-ADDED / SPEC'D SUPPLIER. Spec-in and switching costs give partial
  pricing power; ROCE 20-25% with stickiness. ~19x neighbourhood.
- R4 FRANCHISE / SHARE-OF-WALLET LEADER. Customer capture and repeat
  economics; ROCE 25-30% durable, strong cash. ~21x neighbourhood.
- R5 BRAND / SCARCITY OWNER. Pricing power from brand or structural scarcity;
  ROCE >30%; strategic-premium eligible. ~24x + strategic premium.
Two rules bind the ladder:
- Re-rating engine = the Stage 11 destination-PE delta implied by the rung
  migration; recognition gap = whether current PE already sits at the TO
  rung's neighbourhood. Stage 11 computes; the ladder names.
- Rung-jump base rate: one rung per 2-3 years. A claimed multi-rung leap
  requires extraordinary proof and is itself a red flag.
The alpha the strategy hunts is a real climb of one or more rungs that the
market has not yet repriced (the recognition gap, Part B4).

## TRANSITION DECISION MATRIX (Stage 13 / gate recommendation applies this; adjust via operator ruling only)
Maps the signed model's three state variables to a transition POSTURE. The
posture informs the gate recommendation and the value-trap test; it never
replaces the five-verdict set and never sets a price. The variables:
PROOF GATE (fired / not fired, Part B3), UGLINESS (ARTIFACT-OF-CLIMB /
STRUCTURAL-FEATURE, Part B5), RECOGNITION GAP (open = TO not yet priced /
closed = TO already priced, Part B4, resolved at Stage 11).
- Proof FIRED + ARTIFACT + gap OPEN -> RE-RATING LIVE. The prime setup: the
  climb is proven, the ugly optic is temporary, the market has not repriced.
  Constructive; the BUY still gates on Role 1 valuation and the Hurdle.
- Proof FIRED + ARTIFACT + gap CLOSED -> EARNINGS-ONLY. Climb real but
  already priced; the re-rating engine is spent, returns ride EPS CAGR alone.
  Actionable only if growth clears the Hurdle without help from re-rating.
- Proof NOT FIRED + ARTIFACT + gap OPEN -> RESEARCH / WATCH. Narrative until
  the proof gate fires (Part B3). Not a trade; watch the gate.
- Proof NOT FIRED + ARTIFACT + gap CLOSED -> PRICED NARRATIVE (TRAP). Clean
  optics, transition narrated but unproven, TO state already priced. The most
  seductive cell: no ugliness warns you off, and the downside is double (the
  transition fails AND the multiple compresses). AVOID or hard WATCH with no
  position until the proof gate fires AND the price re-opens the gap.
- Proof NOT FIRED + STRUCTURAL -> VALUE-TRAP RISK. The ugly optic looks
  permanent; classify DEEP WATCH or AVOID unless the classification is
  disproven.
- Proof FIRED + STRUCTURAL -> CONTRADICTION. The gate says climbing, the
  ugliness says decaying; a flag to resolve, not a posture. Re-examine the
  classification before any verdict.
- gap CLOSED + STRUCTURAL -> AVOID. Priced and not really climbing.
State space exhaustive: 2x2x2 = 8 states, all mapped. The two STRUCTURAL rows
each cover both gap states, with gap CLOSED + STRUCTURAL -> AVOID as the
dominating overlay.

## OPERATOR VOICE (STE — all conversation, not only outputs)
Every reply to the operator uses Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100,
codename STE) plus Zinsser. This governs ordinary chat, diagnosis, and
status updates, not only synthesis outputs. Full spec:
Narrative_Writing_Style_v1.md. The load-bearing rules, always on:
- One idea per sentence. 20 words or fewer. Split a long thought in two.
- Active voice. The subject does the action.
- One meaning per word per reply. Plain word over jargon. Gloss a term the
  first time it must appear.
- Cut every word that carries no information ("it is worth noting that",
  "in terms of", "at this point in time").
- No em-dashes or en-dashes as punctuation. Use a full stop, a comma, or
  restructure the sentence.
- No hedging filler (arguably, somewhat, essentially, fundamentally,
  significantly). No AI tells ("not just X but Y", participial openers like
  "Looking at...", empty -ly adverbs, robust/holistic/seamless,
  journey/landscape/ecosystem).
- Numbers first. Say the thing the simplest way that still says it.
Structured blocks keep their format. Tables, scorecards, Section 1B math,
FTTCP verdict cards, YAML, and Notion payloads are not prose. This rule is
silent on them.

## STYLE (synthesis outputs only)
No em-dashes or en-dashes as punctuation. No hyphens in compound
modifiers except tickers/proper nouns. No AI vocabulary. Numbers first.
Symmetric bull-bear. No landing lines. Headline is 6-7 words.

# FILE: `frameworks/Annual_Report_Analysis_Protocol_v1_3.md`

# ROLE 6: ANNUAL REPORT DEEP DIVE PROTOCOL

*Companion to Role 1 (Valuation), Role 2 (Investment Thesis), Role 3 (Devil's Advocate), Role 4 (Quarterly Results Review), Role 5 (Concall Analysis), and Role 7 (FTTCP). Use this protocol every time an Annual Report is released for any company in the active portfolio or watchlist. The AR is the only document of the year where financial, governance, legal, ESG, strategic, and audited disclosures are stitched together. It is also the only document where the Notice of AGM (shareholder resolutions, RPT caps, ESOP grants, special business) is on the record. The AR is therefore the single most important annual artefact for testing — and updating — the investment thesis, and the richest audited evidence feed into the FTTCP catalyst tables.*

*Version 1.3 | Updated 19 August 2026, amended 08 September 2026 | Replaces v1.1 and v1.2 in full. Do not use v1.1, v1.2, or earlier alongside this document.*

*`[08-Sep-2026 amendment: Step 6.5 Second-Order Section added immediately after the Notes triple-pass, per Master Project Prompt v3.7 Rule F (Growth Symmetry companion to Section 1B Amendment 26, operator ruling 08-Sep-2026). Five linkage chains minimum, four questions each, labelled [INFERENCE] required. It sits where it sits because the triple-pass is where the raw material surfaces: the footnote implying demand nobody mentioned, the capex with no stated purpose, the advance from an unnamed customer. Steps 6 and 10 now cross-reference each other on "what was not said". No other step changed.]`*

## INVOCATION

I will trigger this role with one of:

- "Run AR analysis on [Company] FY[YY]"
- "AR deep dive for [Company]"
- "Annual Report review for [Company]"
- Pasting/uploading the AR PDF for an analysed company
- Pasting the Sheet 2 AR Deep Dive output (with triple-pass on notes already done by the pipeline, stage 02)

Run the steps in order. Draw conclusions only after the Notes triple-pass. If the existing Notion thesis is not yet fetched, STOP and fetch it before reading the AR.

## SEQUENCING WITH ROLE 4 (RESULTS REVIEW), ROLE 5 (CONCALL), AND FTTCP

The AR is released 2–3 months after the financial year-end. By the time it arrives, Q4 results and the Q4 concall have already been processed.

- If Role 4 (Q4 Results Review) has been run, the financial mechanics are already in Notion. Role 6 focuses on what only the AR contains:
  - Full Notes to Accounts (vs limited quarterly disclosures)
  - Notice of AGM with special resolutions, including RPT caps for the NEXT financial year
  - Auditor's full report with KAMs, CARO 2020 findings, and EoM/qualifications
  - Board's Report with related party transactions, ESOPs/RSUs granted during the year, and committee composition
  - BRSR (Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report) — governance, social, environmental disclosures
  - Segment reporting in full granularity
  - Promoter shareholding & pledge (formally certified)
  - Subsidiary, associate, JV structure
  - MD&A with industry outlook, strategy, and forward-looking commentary
- If Role 4 has NOT been run for Q4, run Role 4 FIRST, then Role 6. Audited consolidated numbers in the AR will supersede the Q4 filing on any reconciliation difference.
- If a fresh concall happens after the AR is released, run Role 5 after Role 6 and treat any concall commitments as audited (or not) by the AR data.
- **FTTCP interaction (v1.1):** the AR review produces an FTTCP REFRESH GATE (Step 11-PRE). If the AR changes any of the four forward transition verdicts or catalyst strengths, FTTCP is re-run BEFORE any pillar recomputation. Pillar 1 can never be revised from within this protocol directly — the FTTCP ROCE forward verdict is the sole authority (per FTTCP v2.3).

## THE FAILURE MODES THIS PROTOCOL IS DESIGNED TO PREVENT

These are real errors that AR reviews frequently exhibit. Active guard against each:

- **Treating the AR as a marketing brochure.** The MD&A and Chairman's letter are scripted narratives — they tell the story management WANTS told. The thesis-relevant information is in the notes, the auditor's report, the Notice of AGM, and the related party disclosures. Spend at least 70% of analytical effort on these four sections.

- **Skipping the Notice of AGM.** The Notice contains the SHAREHOLDER RESOLUTIONS the Board is asking approval for — including material RPTs, ESOP/RSU plan amendments, capital raises, and changes to directorship. RPT caps are the single most under-read forward-looking signal in any AR. A 100× jump in an RPT cap (vs prior-year actual) is itself the disclosure — even before any concall confirms it.

- **Reading notes as boilerplate.** Notes to Accounts contain accounting policy disclosures, contingent liabilities, ECL methodology, inventory provisions, intangibles capitalisation policy, related party transactions, segment reporting, and additional regulatory information. Every one of these notes can change a thesis assumption. A casual scan is not sufficient — every note must be checked against the thesis. This is the triple-pass discipline.

- **Missing what the auditor flagged.** Key Audit Matters (KAMs) are the auditor's explicit declaration of "this is what could go wrong in this set of financials." A KAM on intangibles under development, on DTA recoverability, on revenue recognition, or on inventory valuation is the auditor telling you exactly where management's judgement could be off. CARO 2020 findings (especially qualifications or adverse remarks) are the auditor telling you where compliance gaps exist. Both must be extracted explicitly, not glossed over.

- **Conflating audited consolidated with management quoted numbers.** Management letters quote selected numbers (often non-GAAP, often standalone, often before exceptional items). The audited consolidated financials are the only authoritative source. When they differ, the audited number wins. Note the gap explicitly — it tells you where management is shaping the narrative.

- **Treating unmodified opinion as "clean across the board."** An unmodified audit opinion only certifies that the financials present a true and fair view IN AGGREGATE. It does not mean every KAM is resolved, every CARO observation is benign, or every contingent liability is small. A clean opinion plus three KAMs plus a CARO observation on inventory plus material contingent liabilities is structurally NOT a clean signal. Read all four layers.

- **Not reading the "what was NOT discussed" list.** A thesis-relevant catalyst that was discussed in three prior concalls but is absent from the AR is information. A risk that the Devil's Advocate predicted would be evaded — and that the AR doesn't address — is information. A peer initiative that should have prompted competitive commentary and didn't — information. Silence is structural in AR analysis, not just in concalls.

- **Missing the segment / geography / customer concentration disclosures.** ARs include segment reporting (sometimes in detail not available in quarterly filings), revenue by geography, and major customer disclosures (where revenue from a single customer exceeds 10% of group revenue). These breakdowns are the strongest test of management's narrative about diversification.

- **Skipping subsidiary/associate disclosures.** Subsidiary performance (especially loss-making subsidiaries) is often disclosed only in the AR. The Board's Report typically contains a paragraph on each subsidiary. Loss-making subsidiaries that get capitalised into the parent or that drag on consolidated cash flow are a recurring quality concern.

- **Not testing R&D capitalisation, intangibles, and DTA aggressiveness.** These are the three line items where Indian accounting allows the most management judgement. An AR where R&D capitalisation has risen, where intangibles under development have grown, AND where DTA balance has grown despite losses is showing three forms of aggressive accounting at once. Each must be tested against the thesis explicitly.

- **Confirmation bias toward existing Notion thesis.** If Notion says BUY/HOLD and the AR reveals weakness, do NOT default to "thesis intact." Read adversarially — every page should be tested against bear-case interpretation first. Let evidence pull you toward bull, never the reverse.

- **Not producing questions for management.** An AR review that ends at "here's what the audited numbers show" is half the work. The other half is "here's what the AR doesn't address that we need answered." These questions feed directly into the next concall or AGM, and the protocol forces extraction of them.

- **Revising Pillar 1 without an FTTCP verdict.** The AR is the document most likely to change the ROCE forward verdict (audited capex commissioning, WC unwind, capital base data). Recomputing destination PE directly from AR data bypasses the FTTCP-before-Role-1 sequencing. The Step 11-PRE gate exists to prevent this.

- **Applying the manufacturing template to a lender.** Cost of Materials, CCC forensics, and CFO/PAT are meaningless for banks, NBFCs, and MFIs. Lending businesses use the LENDER VARIANT tables (Steps 3L, 4L, 5L) and the elevated lender clauses in Step 7.

## STEP 0 — PRE-FLIGHT (MANDATORY)

Before reading the AR, do these in order:

### 0A. Fetch the Notion page (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Use Notion search → fetch on the company name. The thesis IS the anchor for this protocol — without it, you are doing generic AR review, not thesis-testing. Extract and have ready:

- One-line investment thesis (verbatim from Notion)
- Four-pillar destination PE (current values for each pillar, both tracks if dual-track was run)
- Bear/Base/Bull projections (revenue, margin, PAT, EPS) for current FY and next 2–3 FYs
- Thesis-broken conditions (the specific list)
- Quarterly monitoring checklist (the green/red signal table)
- Position size, cost basis, current decision status
- Growth triggers (typically 3–5) with their original confidence ratings
- Devil's Advocate findings (especially what the DA said management would evade, hedge, or fail to deliver)
- Risk matrix (with the warning signals)
- Last Role 4 (Q4 Results Review) output — including the "Questions for Management" table
- Last Role 5 (Concall Analysis) output — including the "What Was NOT Discussed" table AND the Promise-vs-Delivery Tracker with the trailing-4-quarter credibility ratio
- Last FTTCP output — the four forward transition verdicts, catalyst tables, and monitoring triggers
- Promoter Verdict and Management Grade

If Notion has no page for the company, STOP and ask. AR review without a thesis baseline is meaningless and risks fabricating context.

### 0B. Verify position status

Per protocol, before framing ANY analysis with HOLD/ADD/TRIM/EXIT language, ALWAYS verify the current Notion Decision Status:

- BUY NOW / BUY ON DIPS / WATCHLIST / HELD / EXITED / DEPRECATED / AVOID

If status is HELD, also extract Position Size and Average Cost. If status is WATCHLIST, EXITED, or AVOID, frame the analysis around watchlist re-evaluation (the Step 13-W branch), not position management.

### 0C. Identify reporting unit and convention

Look at the column headers and table footnotes in the AR. State explicitly:

- Currency: ₹ Crores / ₹ Lakhs / ₹ Millions / USD / other
- Convert everything to ₹ Crores for analysis (1 Crore = 100 Lakhs = 10 Million)
- State the conversion factor used
- Standalone vs Consolidated: every comparison must specify which. Default analysis is on the CONSOLIDATED financials unless the entity has no subsidiaries.

### 0D. Identify all share-count changes since the prior period

If there has been a stock split, bonus issue, rights issue, ESOP/RSU exercise, QIP, FPO, or buyback in the year, note it explicitly. EPS comparisons are meaningless without share-adjusted figures. Reconcile to the share-count walk usually in the equity section.

### 0E. Confirm sequencing

State explicitly:

- Has Role 4 been run for Q4? If yes, fetch and extract the open questions list and the watchlist items it flagged.
- Has Role 5 been run for the Q4 concall? If yes, fetch the "Questions for Management" and "What Was NOT Discussed" tables and the Promise-vs-Delivery Tracker.
- Has FTTCP been run? If yes, fetch the current four forward verdicts.
- Is a fresh post-AR concall scheduled (e.g., Q1 of new FY)? If yes, this AR review feeds into that concall's question list.

### 0F. Business type check (new in v1.1)

State: **standard operating business** or **lending business** (bank, NBFC, MFI, HFC). Lenders use Steps 3L, 4L, and 5L in place of Steps 3, 4, and 5; the elevated lender clauses in Step 7C; and the lender rows in Step 11A. Their AR data feeds the FTTCP LENDER TRANSITION SET (AUM growth / NIM / asset quality / RoA-RoE) rather than the standard four transitions.

🛑 **STOP. Confirm Notion fetched, thesis extracted, position verified, units identified, share-count changes noted, sequencing established, business type stated. Then proceed.**

Build this exact inventory table before reading any narrative content. This forces a structural understanding of what the AR contains.

**Yellow flags from inventory alone:**

- Promoter pledge increase → RED for governance
- 5+ special resolutions including RPT caps in Notice → high transactional year ahead

▶ **Checkpoint (no wait). Show the inventory and flag any yellow signals. Then continue; the operator reviews it at the Step 11-PRE FTTCP refresh gate.**

## STEP 2 — MANAGEMENT LETTERS & MD&A — CLAIMS & TONE INVENTORY

The Chairman's letter, the MD/CEO letter, and the Management Discussion & Analysis are management's NARRATIVE. They must be inventoried before they are interpreted — otherwise narrative becomes substance by default.

### 2A. Claims Inventory

Build this table by going through the letters and MD&A end-to-end:

| # | Claim | Type | Quantified? | Source Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

**Type categories** (same as Role 5):

- **Backward** — past performance ("Revenue grew 16% YoY")
- **Forward Guidance** — explicit numerical projection ("targeting 25–30% revenue growth in FY27")
- **Forward Soft** — directional but non-numerical ("strong momentum continues")
- **Strategic** — positioning or narrative ("we are India's only…")
- **Operational** — capacity, utilisation, capex, plant
- **Customer/Order** — order book, wins, pipeline
- **Macro/Tailwind** — industry/policy/external

**Quantified?** YES if specific number, date, or binary milestone. NO if hedge or directional.

### 2B. Tone Comparison vs Prior AR

For each major topic, compare the language used in this AR vs the prior year's AR. Build:

| Topic | Prior AR adjective/phrase | This AR adjective/phrase | Direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

**Direction options:** UPGRADED / MAINTAINED / DOWNGRADED / DROPPED / NEW

Examples of meaningful shifts:

- "Demand remains robust" → "Demand has its challenges"
- "Margin expansion expected" → "Margins likely stable"
- "Strong execution on track" → "We are working through some delays"
- A guidance number in prior AR replaced with a directional comment in current AR
- A named customer in prior AR replaced with "leading global telco" in current AR

### 2C. Specificity Score — read jointly with credibility (v1.1)

For the management letters and MD&A combined:

- Number of quantified forward statements
- Number of unquantified forward statements
- Specificity ratio = quantified / total

Benchmark: >0.5 highly specific | 0.3–0.5 moderate | <0.3 heavy hedge language.

**IMPORTANT (v1.1):** high specificity is NOT automatically positive. Combine with the trailing-4-quarter credibility ratio (from the Role 5 tracker fetched in 0A) using the Role 5 Step 6E archetype 2x2: **Committed & Credible** (high/high) / **OVERPROMISER** (high specificity, credibility <60% — the danger quadrant: an AR full of hyper-specific claims from a Grade C/D management is the Overpromiser pattern in its most polished form; treat ALL forward claims as promotional) / **Measured & Credible** (low/high) / **Evasive** (low/low). State the archetype.

### 2D. Mandatory diagnostic questions

- Which of the original Notion growth triggers does the AR explicitly reaffirm? List each.
- Which Notion growth triggers does the AR NOT mention at all? List each (this becomes Step 10 input).
- Has any prior-year commitment from the prior AR been quietly dropped? List each — **each registers as DROPPED in the Promise-vs-Delivery Tracker (Step 12A), with the two-DROPPEDs downgrade rule applying.**
- Has management introduced any NEW growth trigger / catalyst not in the Notion thesis? List with confidence level.
- Has the industry outlook section's tone shifted vs prior AR? In which direction?

▶ **Checkpoint (no wait). Show 2A through 2D. Then continue; the operator reviews it at the Step 11-PRE FTTCP refresh gate.**

## STEP 3 — FULL-YEAR FINANCIAL DECOMPOSITION (RECONCILED TO ROLE 4 IF RUN) — STANDARD BUSINESSES

The AR provides audited consolidated full-year financials. These supersede the Q4 filing. **Lenders skip to Step 3L.**

### 3A. Three-year P&L extraction (mandatory)

| Line Item | FY[YY-2] | FY[YY-1] | FY[YY] | YoY % | 2-yr CAGR |

### 3D. Mandatory diagnostic questions

- Was operating EBITDA growth driven by core operations or by Other Income / PLI / one-offs?
- Is the R&D capitalisation ratio rising, stable, or falling? Rising R&D capitalisation in a loss year is a quality concern.
- Is the effective tax rate consistent with statutory rate? Material gaps indicate either DTA recognition or MAT credit utilisation — flag for Step 6.
- Are D&A and finance costs scaling faster than revenue (capex absorption gap)?
- Is the Expected Credit Loss provision growing materially? Compare ECL as % of revenue across three years.

Record the P&L table, reconciliation, decomposition, and diagnostic answers, then continue to Step 3L or Step 4.

### 4B. Mandatory diagnostic questions

- **Is the CFO a one-off or structural?** If positive CFO came from a single year's receivables unwind (large negative receivable change becoming large positive), it is one-off. If positive CFO came from operating profit + small WC change, it is structural. **State explicitly.**
- **Is the cumulative 3-year CFO/PAT in the band assumed by Pillar 2?** If our valuation assumed 0.65× (structural) and cumulative CFO/PAT is now 0.45×, the pillar has worsened. If cumulative CFO/PAT is now 0.85×, the pillar has improved.
- **Is the FCF positive or negative on a 3-year cumulative basis?** Companies that cumulatively burn cash either dilute, take on debt, or both — neither is good for shareholders.
- **Did capex commission as expected?** If a major capex project was projected to commission, verify with PPE jump matching CWIP decline. State the ₹ amount capitalised. **This is direct audited evidence for the FTTCP ROCE catalyst table — flag it for Step 11-PRE.**
- **What is the Intangibles capex burn rate, and is it normalising or accelerating?** Persistent ₹500+ Cr/year intangible capex is a warning sign — either the company is rebuilding its product platform repeatedly (technology churn) or aggressively capitalising what should be expense.
- **Did the financing cash flow include any disguised equity issuance or debt-raise above the prior year?** Compare net new borrowings vs the change in gross debt on the balance sheet.

▶ **Checkpoint (no wait). Present cash flow table and answers. Then continue; the operator reviews it at the Step 13 position decision.**

### 5B. Working capital forensics

For each WC line item, decompose:

- Receivable days = (Trade Receivables × 365) / Revenue from Sale of Goods
- Inventory days = (Inventory × 365) / Cost of Goods Sold
- Payable days = (Trade Payables × 365) / Cost of Goods Sold
- Cash Conversion Cycle = Receivable + Inventory − Payable days

**Apply the structural vs growth-induced test:**

> *"If this company stopped growing tomorrow, would WC days still be high?"*

If YES → Structural. Pillar 2 assumption should be 0.65×, no growth offset.
If NO → Growth-induced. Pillar 2 assumption is 0.80× with growth offset.

Cite rating agency commentary (CRISIL / ICRA / CARE) if disclosed — they often give the cleanest classification. CARE's structural WC assessment takes precedence over single-year improvements.

## STEP 6 — NOTES TO ACCOUNTS — TRIPLE-PASS (THESIS-ANCHORED)

This is the single highest-value step in AR analysis. Notes contain the disclosures that the management letters and quarterly results cannot summarise away.

If the Sheet 2 (Gemini pipeline) AR Deep Dive output with triple-pass on notes is available, USE it as input — but verify against the AR directly. If the pipeline output is not available, do the triple-pass here.

### Pass 1 — Inventory of all notes

List every numbered note in the financials section. For each:

| Note # | Subject | One-line summary |
| --- | --- | --- |

Standard notes typically include: revenue recognition, PPE, intangibles, inventory, trade receivables & ECL, financial instruments, borrowings, provisions, employee benefits, deferred tax, segment reporting, related party transactions, leases, EPS, contingent liabilities, additional regulatory information, capital management, financial risk management, scheme of amalgamation (if any), subsequent events.

### Pass 2 — Cross-reference to thesis (v1.1 — four-pillar columns)

For each note, mark whether it materially affects any of the following thesis elements:

| Note # | Affects Pillar 1 (ROCE base / FTTCP ROCE forward verdict)? | Affects Pillar 2 (Cash Multiplier / Asset-Quality Multiplier)? | Affects Pillar 3 (Growth Visibility)? | Affects Strategic Premium? | Affects Thesis-Broken Triggers? | Affects Monitoring Checklist? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Mark Y/N for each. Notes affecting capital efficiency trajectory (capex commissioning, WC unwind, capital raises, asset sales) mark Y in the Pillar 1 column and are flagged for the Step 11-PRE FTTCP gate. The notes that mark Y on multiple columns become Pass 3 priorities.

### Pass 3 — Deep-dive on flagged notes

For each flagged note, write a 1–3 paragraph deep-dive. Standard high-priority notes for any company:

#### 6A. Revenue Recognition note

- Does the company recognise revenue at a point in time, over time, or both?
- For long-cycle contracts, what determines milestone billing?
- Are there contract assets (unbilled revenue) growing on the balance sheet? If yes, is this aligned with order book growth?
- Has any revenue been recognised on a "right to invoice" basis where customer payment is contingent?
- Customer advances / deferred revenue — what does the year-end balance imply about FY+1 revenue?

#### 6B. Inventory note

- Inventory composition: raw materials / WIP / finished goods
- Inventory provisions / write-downs: how much in FY[YY] vs prior years? Is this becoming structural (i.e., recurring at similar magnitude)?
- Is there inventory that has been re-classified as "obsolete and written down" while still on the books?
- Inventory days trajectory — is the business getting more or less efficient?

#### 6C. PPE & CWIP note

- Capex during the year — PPE additions
- CWIP balance — what is sitting unfinished?
- Useful lives — any change in estimated useful lives during the year (a change can boost or compress EBITDA artificially)
- Capitalised borrowing cost — how much interest was capitalised vs expensed?
- Capital commitments — what is committed but not yet executed?

#### 6D. Intangibles (incl. under development) note

- What is the composition of "intangibles under development"? (typically: product development costs, technology licenses, software platforms)
- Capitalisation policy — what conditions must be met to capitalise vs expense?
- Annual impairment test outcome — does the company say no impairment is required? (This is mandatory disclosure if an auditor KAM exists on intangibles.)
- Useful lives of intangibles being amortised
- **Most important:** What FY+1, FY+2 revenue / margin / growth assumptions does management use for the impairment test? These are management's INTERNAL projections — compare them against Notion's Four-Pillar projections.

#### 6E. Trade Receivables & ECL note

- Ageing schedule: receivables 0–6m, 6–12m, 1–2y, 2–3y, >3y
- ECL provision matrix — what loss rate is applied at each bucket?
- ECL provision movement during the year (opening + addition − reversal − utilisation = closing)
- Is there a customer-specific provision disclosed (signaling distress with a major customer)?
- Are large receivables (>6 months old) growing or shrinking?

#### 6F. Borrowings note

- Composition by tenor (long-term / short-term) and by nature (term loans / WC loans / buyer's credit / commercial paper)
- Interest rate range and any change in rate vs prior year
- Security — secured against current assets, fixed assets, or unsecured?
- Covenant compliance — any breach during the year? Any covenant disclosed at all?
- Maturity profile — what is due in the next 12 months?

#### 6G. Provisions note

- Warranty provisions — opening, additions, utilisation, closing
- Employee benefits — gratuity, leave encashment, defined benefit obligations
- Litigation / disputed liability provisions
- Any new category of provision introduced during the year (a NEW provision category is a signal of an emerging cost line)

#### 6H. Deferred Tax note

- Deferred Tax Asset composition (on tax losses / depreciation differences / MAT credits)
- Deferred Tax Liability composition
- Net DTA / DTL
- **Recoverability assessment** — management's stated time horizon for utilising tax losses; what level of taxable profit is implied?
- Has DTA been derecognised partially during the year (a partial derecognition is a soft impairment signal)?
- Effective Tax Rate reconciliation — what items cause the gap between statutory and effective rate?

#### 6I. Related Party Transactions note

- List every related party and the transaction value during the year
- Identify any new related party introduced during the year
- For each material RPT, is the value increasing, stable, or decreasing?
- Are there outstanding receivables or payables from/to related parties at year-end?
- Have any RPTs been classified as material (requiring shareholder approval)? If so, is the resolution in the Notice of AGM?

#### 6J. Segment Reporting note

- Reportable segments — has the segment composition changed vs prior year? (A segment change breaks YoY comparability for an entire business line.)
- Segment revenue, profit, and assets per segment
- Geographic revenue split
- Major customer disclosure — any customer contributing >10% of group revenue must be disclosed (with revenue)

#### 6K. Contingent Liabilities & Commitments note

(Already extracted in 5C — here, just ensure every contingent liability is supported by an explanation in the note.)

#### 6L. Additional Regulatory Information note

(Often Note 39 or similar under Indian Ind AS) — Disclosures on:

- Benami property proceedings
- Wilful defaulter declarations
- Transactions with struck-off companies
- Compliance with number of layers of companies
- Utilisation of borrowed funds (no diversion certified)
- Crypto/virtual currency transactions
- Undisclosed income surrendered
- Scheme of arrangements

**Any disclosure other than "Nil" or "Not applicable" here is potentially significant.** Read the specific language.

After completing Pass 1–3, build this synthesis:

| Note # | Why it matters for the thesis | Implication |
| --- | --- | --- |

## STEP 6.5 — SECOND-ORDER SECTION (Master Prompt v3.7, Rule F — MANDATORY)

Runs immediately after the Notes triple-pass, because the triple-pass is where the raw material for the chains surfaces: the footnote that implies expected demand, the capex with no stated purpose, the advance received from a customer not named in the concall.

**What it is.** Minimum FIVE linkage chains. Each chain starts at one growth trigger or one stated fact and traces at least two links out. A chain with no [INFERENCE] in it is a summary, not a chain. Inference is REQUIRED here, labelled, never avoided. The "NOT DISCLOSED" discipline applies to the filed facts at the START of a chain, not to the reasoning that follows them: a chain may not invent a fact, and it must reason from the facts it has.

**Each chain answers four questions.**

| Question | What to look for | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who pays, and why now | Named customer or customer class. What their own filings, capex plans, tender pipelines, or results commentary say about demand for this input | Live web (Claude web): counterparty filings, sector dashboards, policy status |
| What binds | The constraint that decides whether the trigger converts: capacity, working capital, approvals, key hires, a licence, a single supplier | Corpus (Claude Code): capex schedule, WC days, contingent liabilities, related-party notes |
| What moves if it works | Working capital days, margin mix, competitor response, pricing, supplier terms, dilution need | [INFERENCE] from the first two links |
| What was not said | Guidance given on revenue but not on margin. Capex booked with no stated purpose. Hiring or subsidiary formation with no concall mention. Footnotes that imply expected demand (advances received, capacity contracted, forward covers) | Corpus footnotes plus Claude web cross-check |

**Output format, one block per chain.**

```
CHAIN n: [trigger or fact]
Link 1 [tier]: ...
Link 2 [tier]: ...
Link 3 [INFERENCE]: ...
Binding constraint: ...
Unsaid: ...
Observation that confirms or breaks this chain, and confirm-by date: ...
```

Every confirm-by line feeds the Expectation Ledger (Section 1B v3.9 Amendment 23) and the Role 5.5 Downstream Signal Tracker.

**Depth rule.** Five chains is the FLOOR, not the target. Stop when the next chain would repeat a mechanism already traced, not when five is reached.

**Team-workflow split.** The "who pays, and why now" link needs live web and belongs to Claude web. Claude Code drafts every chain from corpus, marks each live-web link PENDING LIVE VERIFICATION, and never fabricates a counterparty fact or pulls one from memory. A chain whose first link is pending is still a chain; it is not deleted, it is marked.

**AR-specific sourcing.** The "what binds" link is answered from this AR: the capex schedule, working-capital days from Step 5, contingent liabilities and related-party notes from Step 6, the auditor's KAMs from Step 7 where they are already read. The "what was not said" link is answered from Step 6 (footnotes) and Step 10 ("what was not discussed"), which now cross-reference each other.

▶ **Checkpoint (no wait). Present the chains. State the count and the reason you stopped (mechanism repetition, not a count). Then continue; the operator reviews it at the Step 13 position decision.**

## STEP 8 — NOTICE OF AGM — RPTs, ESOPs, SPECIAL BUSINESS

The Notice of AGM is the most under-read forward-looking artefact in any AR. It contains the resolutions the Board is asking shareholders to approve — including spending caps, transactional caps, and personnel decisions for the NEXT year.

### 8A. Catalogue of resolutions

| Item # | Type | Description | Approval needed | Material? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

**Types:**

- Ordinary Business (adoption of financials, declaration of dividend, re-appointment of director retiring by rotation, ratification of auditors)
- Special Business: Material RPT approval
- Special Business: ESOP / RSU / SAR plan amendments
- Special Business: Capital raise (FPO / QIP / Rights / Preferential)
- Special Business: Increase in borrowing limits (Section 180)
- Special Business: Increase in authorised share capital
- Special Business: Investment / loans (Section 186) beyond limits
- Special Business: Re-appointment of MD / CEO / WTD with remuneration
- Special Business: Appointment / re-appointment of Independent Director
- Special Business: Amendments to AoA / MoA
- Special Business: Buyback / Bonus / Stock split

### 8B. Material RPT analysis (highest priority)

For each material RPT resolution, extract:

| Related Party | Nature of Transactions | FY[YY] Actual (₹ Cr) | FY[YY+1] Cap Requested (₹ Cr) | Multiple of Actual | Implied Forward Activity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

**The "Multiple of Actual" column is the single most important forward signal:**

- 1.0× to 1.5× — Routine carry-forward, no signal
- 1.5× to 3× — Modest growth expectation
- 3× to 10× — Material scale-up expected
- >10× — Step-change expected. Management is anticipating a TRANSFORMATIVE year.

**For high-multiple resolutions, ask:**

- Does the implied scale-up match (or exceed) the Notion thesis revenue projection?
- Does it imply a specific catalyst is expected to fire? **If yes, this is documented (📄) forward evidence — flag it for the FTTCP catalyst tables in Step 11-PRE.**
- Is there a corresponding capex or capacity disclosure?

### 8C. ESOP / RSU resolutions

If there is an ESOP/RSU resolution, extract:

- Number of new options / RSUs to be granted in FY+1 (if specified)
- Total pool size as % of paid-up share capital
- Exercise price methodology (market / discount / par)
- Vesting period and conditions
- Implied dilution % if fully exercised

Compare against:

- Notion's projected EPS — does the implied dilution change the share count assumption?
- Promoter holding — does the dilution erode promoter holding below thesis-relevant thresholds?

### 8D. Capital allocation resolutions

Any resolution authorising:

- New borrowing limits (under Section 180)
- New investment limits (under Section 186)
- Issue of equity / convertibles
- Buyback

These are forward signals on cash needs / cash deployment. Compare against the Notion projection of net debt trajectory and free cash flow profile. For lenders, compare capital raise authorisations against the CRAR trajectory and growth guidance.

### 8E. Director / KMP resolutions

Extract:

- Re-appointment of MD / CEO / WTD — note remuneration package and any changes
- Appointment of new Independent Director — note the director's background and experience
- Re-appointment of director retiring by rotation — note who and any board committee changes

▶ **Checkpoint (no wait). Present 8A through 8E. The Material RPT table is the single most important forward indicator in the AR. Then continue; the operator reviews it at the Step 13 position decision.**

**Silence interpretation hierarchy:**

## STEP 10.5 — DOWNSTREAM SIGNAL TRACKER — ANNUAL CROSS-CHECK (v1.2 addition)

The consolidated Downstream Signal Tracker (Notion database peer to COMPANIES MASTER, established at initial workup via Master Project Prompt v3.7 Role 5.5) is refreshed monthly via the Role 5.5 Monthly Refresh Workflow. The quarterly reviews (Role 4 v1.4 Step 5.5) reconcile target-company reported numbers against tracker rows for THIS company. The AR is the once-a-year checkpoint for tracker maintenance — the annual cross-check where signals may need to be added, retired, or reconciled against the AR's own audited customer-concentration disclosure.

**Tracker coordinates (LIVE — use directly, do not search):** Database URL https://app.notion.com/p/ea5f02670d114b2abd7b74f88bb33061 | Data source ID `926b65ce-ddd2-4d8b-8eae-05e66b6f6c9f`

The annual cross-check catches three failure modes the monthly and quarterly cadences alone can miss:

- **Signal decay.** A downstream signal that was material 12 months ago (a named end-customer molecule, a specific counterparty partnership) may have quietly dropped off management's own commentary. The AR is the annual audit of "does this signal still matter?"
- **New signals disclosed only annually.** ARs sometimes name a customer or partnership for the first time (Segment note, Related Party note, Board's Report subsidiary paragraph). Any such disclosure must be added to the tracker via Role 5.5 Case A/B procedure.
- **Reconciliation with audited customer concentration.** Customers exceeding 10% of group revenue are named in the AR. If the tracker has been carrying a signal for "big-name partner X" but the AR's customer-concentration disclosure names Y instead, the tracker is stale and the mapping must be corrected.

### 10.5A. Pull tracker rows for this company

Query the Downstream Signal Tracker for all rows where Affected Companies includes THIS company. For each row, answer:

| Signal (from tracker) | Still material per AR? | Latest AR-implied direction | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Signal 1] | Yes / No / Ambiguous | Confirms / Neutral / Threatens | Retain / Retire / Downgrade |
| [Signal 2] | ... | ... | ... |
| [Signal 3] | ... | ... | ... |

A signal is "still material" if the AR's segment reporting, MD&A, customer disclosure, or Notice of AGM references either the signal directly or the customer/product it tracks. A signal that has vanished from the AR's own text is an amber flag for the thesis; a signal that was material and remains prominent is a green flag; a signal explicitly downgraded (e.g., "moving away from concentration to customer X") is a red flag for that specific thesis element.

### 10.5B. New downstream signals disclosed in this AR

Every signal that appears in this AR for the first time and is materially relevant to the forward thesis must be added to the tracker via Role 5.5 Case A/B procedure:

| New Signal | Where in the AR (page ref) | Primary Source URL (external, not the AR itself) | Cadence | Case A/B | Rationale for Adding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Common sources of new signals discovered only in ARs:
- Segment reporting note listing a customer or geography not previously visible in quarterly filings
- Related Party Transactions section naming a formerly-undisclosed counterparty
- Board's Report subsidiary paragraphs naming a foreign JV partner
- Notice of AGM special business seeking approval for an exclusive supply arrangement
- MD&A section naming a specific product / molecule / platform for the first time

For each new signal, populate the tracker with a primary-source URL that is NOT the AR itself (the AR is a lagging indicator; the tracker maintains forward-looking sources).

### 10.5C. Reconciliation with audited customer concentration

Extract the AR's customer-concentration disclosure — typically Note 46 or 47 or a segment note — listing customers exceeding 10% of group revenue. Then verify:

| Audited Customer (from AR) | % of Revenue | Corresponding Tracker Signal | Signal Health |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Customer name] | ___% | [Tracker signal that tracks this customer] or "MISSING FROM TRACKER" | Confirms / Stale / Missing |

If an AR-disclosed 10%+ customer has no corresponding tracker signal, the tracker is incomplete and a new signal must be added under 10.5B. If a tracker signal claims to track a customer that no longer appears in the AR's 10%+ list, either the concentration has fallen (positive: diversification) or the customer relationship has ended (negative: thesis erosion) — the reconciliation must state which.

### 10.5D. Update the consolidated Downstream Signal Tracker

At the end of Step 10.5, the tracker rows relevant to this company are updated in place:

- Retired signals: struck through with reason (customer no longer disclosed / product discontinued / partnership ended); Affected Companies field for this company removed
- New signals: added with primary sources via Role 5.5 Case A/B procedure
- Direction updates: refreshed against the annual observation
- Per-Company Thesis Element: updated if the AR revealed a change in what the signal now tests

The updated tracker becomes the input to the next monthly refresh cycle and to the next quarterly Step 5.5 reconciliation for this company.

## STEP 13 — POSITION DECISION

**Verify Decision Status from 0B before applying this logic.** Use the H-branch for HELD names and the W-branch for everything else.

### 13-H. Decision logic — HELD positions

```
IF any thesis-broken condition has FIRED (Step 11D):
    → EXIT immediately at market
    → Note exit rationale and reclassify to EXITED in Notion

ELSE IF the position is in MOMENTUM bucket (chandelier exit governs):
    → HOLD unless chandelier triggered
    → AR analysis informs FUTURE re-entry sizing only
    → Do NOT convert momentum position to value position based on AR

ELSE IF audited actual lands BELOW BEAR case on 2+ key metrics:
    → Trim 25–50% based on severity
    → Apply the annual probability re-weighting rule (one notch toward Poor, immediate)
    → Update thesis with downward revision
    → Reclassify (BUY → WATCHLIST → DEPRECATED) per discipline

ELSE IF actual lands BETWEEN BEAR and BASE:
    → Hold existing position
    → Tighten add-back triggers for any incremental sizing
    → Update Notion projections with downward revision

ELSE IF actual lands AT or ABOVE BASE:
    → Hold or add per existing entry / MoS rules
    → Confirm Four-Pillar inputs still valid (post Step 11-PRE / 11A)
    → Document the upgrade rationale in Notion
```

**OVERLAY — AR-specific veto rules (apply regardless of branch):**

- KAM-disclosed soft assets > 50% of equity → tighten monitoring; consider adding to thesis-broken triggers
- Modified audit opinion / EoM paragraph → AVOID overlay, full re-thesis required
- Going Concern flag → IMMEDIATE EXIT regardless of position bucket
- Material weakness in IFC opinion → trim 50%, full re-thesis required
- Multiple promoter pledge increases → downgrade Promoter Verdict by one band
- Three consecutive years of cash losses (CARO xvii) → AVOID overlay
- For lenders: RBI supervisory action or penalty disclosed → AMBER minimum, full governance re-check; credit cost above guided band with provisioning release flattering PAT → Pillar 2L band biases down one level

### 13-W. Decision logic — WATCHLIST / non-held names (new in v1.1)

```
IF any thesis-broken condition has FIRED:
    → Reclassify to AVOID; record the specific reversal conditions for any future re-entry

ELSE IF audited actual lands BELOW BEAR on 2+ key metrics:
    → Apply the annual probability re-weighting rule
    → Revise projections down; recompute entry zone and MoS price
    → Push the master decision gate out; state the new gate explicitly

ELSE IF actual lands BETWEEN BEAR and BASE:
    → Revise projections down; recompute entry zone; update Notion

ELSE IF actual lands AT or ABOVE BASE:
    → Confirm or tighten the entry zone
    → If a pre-committed BUY gate threshold was met by audited data, state it explicitly and recommend the pre-committed action
```

No trim/exit mechanics for non-held names. The W-branch output is always: updated entry zone, updated gate, updated Decision Status if warranted.

### 13A. Trim / Add Trigger Refinement

If the AR introduces new information about execution quality, capacity utilisation, customer mix, or governance, state explicitly:

- Original add-back trigger (from Notion) / Revised add-back trigger (if different)
- Original trim ladder (from Notion) / Revised trim ladder (if different)

### 13B. Updated entry / Margin of Safety price

If destination PE has been recomputed in Step 11A, recompute:

- Year 3 fair value (Bear / Base / Bull), both tracks if dual-track applies
- Probability-weighted fair value (with the corrected credibility-grade weights from 12A)
- Entry price = exit-consistent fair value ÷ (1 + tier hurdle)³ (Tier A 1.25, Tier B 1.20), shown with the Amendment 19 FV CAGR and return-source label
- Margin of Safety per the Master evidence scale (20%/30%/40%), or as position size for fast-growth names (Section 1B v3.9 Amendment 25; operator ruling OR-18, 2026-10-04)
- Update Notion with the revised price band

### 13C. Single cleanest metric for Q1 of next FY

Identify the ONE metric that most cleanly resolves the bull/bear case for the next quarter:

- "[Segment] sales line item — if Q1 FY27 clears ₹X Cr, the add-on PO is effectively firing"

- "Net Debt — if Q1 FY27 net debt is > ₹X Cr, WC death spiral risk is materialising"
- Lenders: "Credit cost vs guided band" is the default candidate

Pick exactly one. State it. State the bull threshold and the bear threshold.
